security_spec.violation_condition: The XiangShan RTL is synthesized or configured such that M-mode (Machine mode, the highest privilege level) is either absent from the privilege architecture, unreachable after reset, or its privileged access rights are not enforced as the maximum authority level. This includes: (a) the hart resetting into a privilege mode other than M-mode, (b) the CSR module failing to instantiate M-mode-only CSRs (e.g., mstatus, mtvec, mepc, mcause, mtval, mie, mip, medeleg, mideleg, pmpcfg*, pmpaddr*), (c) the instruction decoder rejecting or mishandling M-mode-privileged instructions (MRET, WFI when implemented, SFENCE.VMA in M-mode context), or (d) the privilege-level state register (priv_mode in the processor core) being hardwired to a non-M-mode value or lacking the M-mode encoding entirely.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: PRIVILEGE_ANCHOR_MISSING — The hardware fails to implement the mandatory highest-privilege anchor (M-mode), resulting in a flat privilege hierarchy where every execution context operates at the same effective privilege level. This is a catastrophic architectural vulnerability class that manifests in XiangShan RTL through: (a) Reset vector misconfiguration — the reset state machine in the core's control unit initializes priv_mode to a non-M value, or the mtvec CSR is not properly initialized at reset, causing the first instruction fetch to execute in an unauthorized privilege context. (b) CSR decode gating bugs — the combinational logic in CSR.scala that gates CSR read/write access based on current priv_mode uses incomplete or incorrectly enumerated privilege-level checks, allowing lower-privilege access to M-mode-only CSR fields. (c) PMP enforcement bypass — the PMP checker is instantiated but its enable/disable state or address-matching logic is not gated by M-mode authority; any hart can reconfigure PMP entries because there is no distinction between the configuring agent and the enforcing agent. (d) Trap delegation loop — mideleg/medeleg are writable from non-M-mode, allowing untrusted code to create delegation cycles where traps bounce between privilege levels without ever reaching a trusted handler, leading to denial of service or controlled trap suppression. (e) Instruction privilege check omission — the decoder's privilege-check logic for M-mode-only instructions (MRET, SFENCE.VMA) does not verify that current priv_mode == M, allowing these instructions to execute from S-mode or U-mode and enabling unauthorized privilege transitions. (f) Multi-hart inconsistency — in a multi-core XiangShan configuration, M-mode is present on some harts but absent or misconfigured on others, creating asymmetric trust domains where the compromisable harts can attack the trusted harts through shared cache-coherent memory or inter-hart interrupts without M-mode-level mediation.
affected_entities: [CSR Module] CSR.scala — priv-level access gating for all M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mtvec, mepc, mcause, mtval, mie, mip, medeleg, mideleg, mcycle, minstret, mhartid, marchid, mimpid, mvendorid, mscratch, mtinst, mtval2, pmpcfg*, pmpaddr*, mcounteren, menvcfg, mseccfg); reset state initialization of M-mode CSR fields. [PMP Checker] PMPChecker.scala — PMP rule enforcement depends on M-mode being the only configuration authority; PMP lock bits (L bit in pmpcfg) have no meaning without M-mode exclusivity. [Trap/Interrupt Controller] Control.scala / Trap.scala — trap delegation logic (medeleg/mideleg routing), exception priority encoding, MRET execution privilege check, privilege mode transition state machine. [Instruction Decoder] IDU.scala / Decoder.scala — privilege-check logic for MRET, WFI, SFENCE.VMA, and any future M-mode-privileged instructions; must reject these instructions when priv_mode != M. [TLB/PTW] TLB.scala / PTW.scala — page-table walker privilege mode context; SFENCE.VMA authority; virtual memory isolation depends on M-mode being able to invalidate TLB entries across all address spaces. [Reset Controller] Reset.scala / Boot.scala — reset vector configuration, initial priv_mode assignment at hart reset, CSR reset state sequencing. [Multi-Core Interconnect] — IMSIC/PLIC interrupt routing, cache coherence protocol privilege tagging, inter-hart interrupt (MSI) delivery, debug module cross-hart access control.
security_spec.summary: PR #2413 introduces normative rule 'mmode_req' mandating that all hardware implementations must provide M-mode as the highest privilege level with unfettered machine access. From the XiangShan RTL hardware security audit perspective, this single rule is the foundational requirement upon which all other privilege-based isolation mechanisms depend. If XiangShan were to violate this rule—by omitting M-mode, hardwiring priv_mode to a lower privilege, or failing to enforce M-mode exclusivity for privileged CSR access and instruction execution—the entire RISC-V security architecture collapses: PMP becomes meaningless, CSR access control dissolves, trap delegation is subvertible, and no trusted execution anchor exists. The affected hardware modules span the CSR unit, PMP checker, trap/interrupt controller, instruction decoder, TLB/PTW, reset controller, and multi-core interconnects. Verification of this rule requires confirming that priv_mode resets to M-mode, all M-mode CSR fields are only writable when priv_mode == M, M-mode-privileged instructions trap when executed from lower modes, and PMP configuration is exclusively an M-mode operation. This is priority-critical for XiangShan security assurance.
